names.name: 'khor 'das dbyer med — the inseparability of saṃsāra and nirvāṇa
kun gzhi rgyu rgyud — the all-base causal continuum
gsal stong zung 'jug — the union of clarity and emptiness
Mahāmudrā, the result continuum (phyag rgya chen po 'bras bu'i rgyud)
spros bral — freedom from elaborations (Madhyamaka, as in Gorampa)
śūnyatā

descriptions: The all-base (ālaya) as causal continuum holds saṃsāra and nirvāṇa both (Vajra Verses, Derge 139b.1).
The result is Mahāmudrā, the result continuum, known through the four result-empowerments as omniscience (Vajra Verses 139b.2–3).
Pure vision: the inexhaustible ornamental wheel of the Sugatas' body, speech and mind (Vajra Verses 139a.7).
The ultimate is free from the four extremes of existence, non-existence, both and neither (Gorampa, Distinguishing the Views).
negations: not merely the absence of inherent existence (Gorampa, against Tsongkhapa)
not an other-empty permanent entity (Gorampa, against Dolpopa)
'If grasping arises, it is not the view' (Parting from the Four Attachments, line 4)
relation_to_self: The individual mind-stream as ālaya is the causal continuum in which the result is present as potential; realizing its clarity-emptiness frees it from the self-grasping of the impure vision.
relation_to_world: The three visions: the world as seen by beings with afflictions (impure), by yogins in meditation (experiential), and by buddhas (pure) — one reality appearing according to the purity of mind.
caveat: Sakya teachers would reject any reading of 'inseparability of saṃsāra and nirvāṇa' as a substantial one-reality behind appearances; Gorampa's freedom from elaboration denies even that emptiness is an entity. The Lamdre view is realized through empowerment and the two stages, not by reasoning alone.

names.name: don dam bden pa (ultimate truth), one only
chos nyid (dharmatā)
stong pa nyid (emptiness)
ultimate bodhicitta

descriptions: The ultimate is one; others hold it to be two; dharmatā, established as nothing at all, cannot be two or three (Satyadvayāvatāra 4).
Without arising or ceasing; free of thing and non-thing; inexpressible, unconditioned; realizing it the yogin abandons the afflictive and cognitive obscurations (Satyadvayāvatāra 5–9).
Wisdom is knowing the emptiness of own-nature of aggregates, elements and sense-bases as unborn (Bodhipathapradīpa v48).
negations: no arising from self, other, both or without cause (Bodhipathapradīpa v50)
not found when analysed as one or many (Bodhipathapradīpa v51)
seeing it is 'not seeing'; no seer and nothing seen (Satyadvayāvatāra 7)
relation_to_self: Selflessness of persons and phenomena; the practitioner meditates on selflessness without conceptualization (Bodhipathapradīpa v54–55).
relation_to_world: Conventional truth is of two kinds, false and correct; correct conventional truth is what, unexamined, arises and ceases and can perform functions; it is to be respected — cause and effect, virtue and vice — and is the ladder to the ultimate (Satyadvayāvatāra 2–3, 18–22).
caveat: Atiśa's 'the ultimate is one' denies that the ultimate is divisible, not that it is a single substance: it is dharmatā 'not established as anything'. A reading of it as a positive one-reality would be rejected.

names.name: stong pa nyid — emptiness of inherent existence (rang bzhin gyis stong pa)
don dam bden pa — ultimate truth
med dgag — non-affirming negation
rten 'brel — dependent arising, the king of reasons
ngo bo nyid sku — the nature body (svābhāvikakāya)
'od gsal — the clear light (in Highest Yoga Tantra)

descriptions: The mere absence of inherent existence — of existence from the object's own side — in every phenomenon (Lamrim Chenmo, insight section).
Emptiness and dependent arising are one intention: because things arise dependently they are empty, and because empty they can arise (Three Principal Aspects 10–13; Praise of Dependent Origination).
The ultimate truth is an object of knowledge, found by a reasoning consciousness analysing the final mode of being.
negations: the object of negation is inherent existence, not conventional existence — negating too much falls into nihilism, too little into eternalism
emptiness is not an other-empty permanent absolute (against Dolpopa)
no ālaya-vijñāna and no reflexive awareness even conventionally (eight difficult points)
relation_to_self: The self exists merely as designated in dependence on the aggregates; the innate apprehension of an inherently existent self is the root of saṃsāra, cut only by the wisdom realizing its emptiness.
relation_to_world: The world exists conventionally, validly established by conventional valid cognition; cause and effect are 'unfailing' and fully compatible with emptiness.
caveat: Gelug holds that each phenomenon has its own emptiness (though all emptinesses are of one taste) and that emptiness is itself empty; it rejects any positive, self-existent absolute (shentong, Advaita's Brahman). It would accept 'one truth, many names' only for the single mode of being of all phenomena — their emptiness — not for a substance or a divine person.

phyag rgya chen po — Mahāmudrā: sūtra Mahāmudrā as emptiness, mantra Mahāmudrā as the clear light of great bliss
sems kyi gnas lugs — the abiding nature of mind

descriptions: The conventional nature of mind is clarity and knowing; its ultimate nature is its emptiness of inherent existence (Highway of the Conquerors, as the Gelug Mahāmudrā teaches).
Many names — co-emergent union, amulet box, fivefold, one taste, four letters, pacification, Chöd, Dzogchen, Madhyamaka view — converge in one intent (Highway of the Conquerors).
caveat: The 'one intent' is the emptiness of mind as the Gelug understands it (a non-affirming negation); the convergence statement is not a claim that the schools' views are identical in every detail.
